sections.title: The Dog and the Tortoise

dialogue.line: Once upon a time, a tortoise called out a dog for a race.

dialogue.speaker: Tortoise
dialogue.line: I can run faster than you.

dialogue.speaker: Dog
dialogue.line: You? You must be joking! Even in my sleep, you cannot run faster than me.

The tortoise planned to prepare large chunks of delicious meat with fat bones. He deliberately dropped the pieces of meat along the paths of the race thinking that the dog would smell the meat and get attracted to them.

illustrations: A large dog standing next to a small tortoise on a green field

sections.title: The Race

dialogue.line: On the day of their race, the other animals gathered to watch the most interesting race. As soon as the race started, the dog flew past the tortoise with high speed while the tortoise picked his steps as slowly and clumsily as he could.
Soon, the dog saw a chunk of meat on the way.

dialogue.speaker: Dog
dialogue.line: I will take a bite of this tasty meat before that slowcoach comes here.

As soon as he finished eating that meat, a few paces ahead he saw another piece on his path. So he slowed down and stopped to eat each piece. When the dog finally reached the finishing line, he met the tortoise there. He was surprised to see the tortoise before him and all the other animals praising the tortoise for winning the race.

illustrations: The tortoise at the finish line surrounded by other animals, the dog arriving in surprise

sections.title: Okon and Akan

dialogue.line: Once upon a time Okon, a farmer, went to check his traps. As he went near one of the traps, he noticed something caught in the trap which he could not see clearly. He called his friend, Akan, to help him remove the catch from the trap. Akan realised that the animal in the trap was a large snake which had gone to hide behind the stem of the trap.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: It is a large snake and this type spits!

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: The trap caught it by the tail!

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: Then catch it by the head.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: Do you want it to bite me?

illustrations: Two men (Okon and Akan) standing near a wooden fence by a small building

sections.title: Okon and Akan (continued)

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: This snake does not bite, it only spits into people's eyes.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: Oh, ho! You want me to be blind? It is your trap. So go ahead and take your catch.

dialogue.speaker: Okon
dialogue.line: I know now that you are not a good friend.

dialogue.speaker: Akan
dialogue.line: You are a true friend who wants me to be hurt.
The two men stood there looking at the large beast until it struggled out of the trap and crawled away into the jungle.

questions: What job does Okon do?
Who was his friend?
What did the trap catch?
Why did Okon ask Akan to remove it from the trap?
Who do you think is a true friend in the story?
What is the moral of the story?

sections.title: Kabir and the Black Bag

dialogue.line: One bright morning, Kabir was going to his father's farm near which is located near their thatched house. On his way to the farm, he was thinking of the number of yam heaps he would have to make before noon. Then he would have to quickly bathe and rush to the local school that usually start at three.
He did not know if his mother would be able to give him food that day. He was only sure of the meal in the evening.

illustrations: Kabir walking to the farm, thinking about yams

questions: When was Kabir going to the farm?
What did he want to do there?
When would he return home?
Where would he go after returning from the farm?
What did he see under the leaves?
Why did he check the bag?
Why did he not take the bag home?
Why were the policemen amazed?
How did the owner of the bag pay Kabir back?
What did you learn from this story?
sections.title: The Black Bag

dialogue.line: Before Kabir went to the big kolanut tree that was very closeby to his father's farm, he noticed a black bag under the low leaves beside the path.
He ran to the farm without looking back. When he was coming back, he noticed that the black bag was still there.
It must belong to someone. He must have been forgotten there. I must see what is inside. Perhaps I can get a clue of who the owner is.
dialogue.speaker: Kabir

dialogue.line: Kabir carefully opened the bag and found bundles of money neatly tied together with strong strings. He had never seen that much money in his entire life. He picked the bag and ran to the police station to handover the bag with money. The policemen were amazed at the honesty of a poor boy. Soon, the police found the owner of the bag. The man was so pleased with Kabir that he decided to pay his school fees.

illustrations: Kabir finding a black bag under leaves
Kabir handing the bag to the police

sections.title: The Caterpillar and its Palace (Story)

dialogue.line: Once upon a time, all the animals used to live together. One day they found a palace in the jungle that they thought that nobody was living in it. The big animals like lions, tigers, hippopotamuses, elephants, and even smaller animals like the antelopes and squirrels started to argue among themselves about who was the most powerful and the bravest and the fittest to live in the palace.
As they continued to argue, they heard a loud voice from the palace saying;

I have ridden on elephants and rhinoceroses and lions and tigers and have broken their backs. I have proved to them that they are not as strong as they claimed. And the birds are afraid of me even though they can fly, I make their lives miserable if they come close to me. And so, if you dare enter this palace, be prepared for your death. But if you wish to dare death, make sure you do not come inside the palace with any bird.
dialogue.speaker: Voice

illustrations: Animals outside a palace in the jungle

sections.title: The Caterpillar (Conclusion)

dialogue.line: The animals got frightened. They all ran away and did not live together again. From that day onwards, the caterpillar lived peacefully all alone in its big palace, the cocoon.

sections.title: The Sleeping Old Lilly

dialogue.line: Mark and Lilly have lived in the same street for over thirty years. Now they both are seventy years old, and now they talk about the good things they have done for their town.

One day, there was a heavy rain in the village. Mark thought that his friend, Lilly had gone to the farm. He rushed off to the farm without checking if Lilly was at home.
